Additional information at 31 December 2025:

1. Inventory was valued at US\$13,940.
2. Equipment is depreciated at 10% per annum on cost and the delivery van at 25% per annum on the reducing balance.
3. The loan was taken out on 1 January 2025 at 8% interest per annum.
4. Insurance of US\$355 was prepaid. Commission received included US\$280 for January 2026.
5. A debt of US\$580 is irrecoverable. The allowance for irrecoverable debts is to be 5% of the remaining trade receivables.
6. Rudo took goods costing US\$765 for her own use.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the increase in the allowance for irrecoverable debts.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.
parts.explanation: Other income: commission 2,700 − 280 = 2,420; discount received 845. Expenses: loan interest 480 + 64 = 544; insurance 1,880 − 355 = 1,525; irrecoverable debts 430 + 580 = 1,010; allowance increase 271; depreciation 2,300 + 3,775; plus wages, rent, heating and lighting and general expenses; total 35,260. Profit 46,865 + 3,265 − 35,260 = 14,870.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Other income: commission 2,700 − 280 = 2,420; discount received 845. Expenses: loan interest 480 + 64 = 544; insurance 1,880 − 355 = 1,525; irrecoverable debts 430 + 580 = 1,010; allowance increase 271; depreciation 2,300 + 3,775; plus wages, rent, heating and lighting and general expenses; total 35,260. Profit 46,865 + 3,265 − 35,260 = 14,870.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the total current liabilities at 31 December 2025.
parts.explanation: Trade payables 10,560 + other payables: loan interest 64 + commission in advance 280 = 10,904. The loan is a non-current liability.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Trade payables 10,560 + other payables: loan interest 64 + commission in advance 280 = 10,904. The loan is a non-current liability.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Rudo's lender has offered her a small discount if she repays the whole loan of US\$6,800 now. Advise Rudo whether she should do so. Justify your answer using figures from the statements.

points.description: Bank balance 3,870 is far less than 6,800: repayment would need an overdraft or the sale of assets
Paying with the whole bank balance plus an overdraft would cut the acid test from 1.55 : 1 to about 0.94 : 1, leaving too little to pay trade payables of 10,560
Conclusion: do not repay now (or repay part later when receivables are collected); the interest of 544 a year is easily covered by a profit of 14,870

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She should not repay the loan now. Her bank balance is only US\$3,870, about half of the US\$6,800 needed, so she would have to use all her cash and borrow the rest on overdraft. Her acid test would fall from 1.55 : 1 to about 0.94 : 1, and she could struggle to pay trade payables of US\$10,560. The interest of US\$544 a year is easily covered by her profit of US\$14,870. She could repay part of the loan later, once more receivables have been collected.

parts.explanation: Use liquidity figures and the interest cost.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: A supplier in Harare offers to supply identical bags at US\$34 each. Tatenda's production cost per bag is US\$36.45 (to the nearest cent). The supervisor's wages, factory rent and machinery depreciation would continue if he stopped making bags. Advise Tatenda whether to accept the offer.

points.description: Buying looks cheaper per bag than the full production cost
But fixed factory costs of 30,600 continue, so the cost actually saved per bag is only about US\$28.80, less than US\$34
Conclusion: continue to make the bags (also consider quality, reliability of supply, staff)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: He should keep making the bags. The offer of US\$34 is below the full cost of US\$36.45, but supervisor's wages, factory rent and depreciation (US\$30,600) would still be paid. Only about US\$28.80 per bag would be saved, so buying in would cost more than it saves. He would also lose control over quality and depend on one supplier.

parts.explanation: Compare the buying price with the costs that would actually be saved.
